Prompts: REA_17 §3.4. · edge (catalyst pole only; owner 2026-10-16, THE EDGE v9: two sentences, the energy and its three ruling domains from the GOD table, then a clause per domain in The Pattern's voice; the metric; the head derived in the app)

candidates.structural_interaction: Warmth meeting warmth cross-polarity — presence competing with presence
candidates.k2_overview: Your Fire moves as the Rival: flame that leaps between torches. You catch ambition from the people around you and pass yours back doubled, the most contagious energy in any gathering. Stakes make you luminous. The same draft that spreads your fire can spread it thin, so choose which blazes are actually yours.
candidates.k2_functional: Your energy flares with company and stakes, then needs true dark to recover.

k2_domain_readings.Rivalry: Your rivals are accelerants: nothing focuses your flame like a nearby blaze. Keep rivalry ritual, races and games and friendly scoreboards, so the heat builds camaraderie instead of ash.
k2_domain_readings.Shared stakes: You fund and join easily, splitting bills and risks in the same warm gesture. Enthusiasm signs faster than judgment reads. Let every shared blaze get one cold morning review before you pour fuel.
k2_domain_readings.Boldness: Your boldness ignites others, which multiplies its consequences. Lead the charges worth leading. A spark that picks its tinder builds bonfires. One that does not builds regrets.

catalyst.define: Running thin, the reserve is small and needs a contest to light it. Your heat comes most easily from someone else's.

angles.drive: You rise to a dare before deciding if you want it. You wake in a contest like nowhere else, so you weigh the rival more than the stakes. With you in the race, everyone runs faster.
angles.cost_self: Rising to a dare tells you that you are in the game. You would sooner take a test than take a break, so rest never comes first. Your body pays for every race, including the ones you won.
angles.cost_others: You take up a friend's dare at full speed, before they can laugh it off. Winning in front of them matters more than keeping it friendly, so you play every round for keeps. Nothing with you is ever just a game.

angles.drive: Other people's ambition is the kind you catch most easily. You catch a rival's goal faster than you find your own, so you run on borrowed wanting rather than wait. What you are hungry for is a contest worth your whole heart.
angles.cost_self: Catching ambition is quicker than growing it, and you know it. You go after what a rival chases before asking what you want yourself, because wanting alone feels thin. Some of your hardest wins were for things you never cared about.
angles.cost_others: You catch a friend's plan before they finish the sentence. Running their race feels better than cheering from the side, so you turn their goal into a shared one. The win they pictured alone ends up with you in it.

angles.drive: On a shared bet, you go all in before anyone asks. Holding back feels like not being there, so you put in your money before reading the terms. Your friends never have to wonder whose side you are on.
angles.cost_self: Being all in is how you show you mean it. You put money where your friends are rather than where your sense is, because holding back feels worse than losing. Your savings rise and fall with the plans of the people you love.
angles.cost_others: With someone you like, you go all in without being asked. You would rather add your own money than check whether they wanted it, and you double what they put in. Their plan ends up bigger and riskier than the one they made.

friction.define: Running over, your strength hunts for a contest in everything. Your need to stay ahead burns through rest and friendship alike.

angles.drive: Losing stays with you far longer than winning does. A rival's win feels like something taken from you, and you set out to get it back. You turn every friendly game into a fight and miss the fun of playing.
angles.cost_self: Hating to lose keeps you in every contest long after it stops paying. You would sooner stay in a losing race than be the first to step off, so you stay. For every race you refuse to leave, you give up a night of sleep.
angles.cost_others: Whenever a friend pulls ahead, you hate it before you are glad. You hear their good news as lost ground, so you answer it with news of your own instead of just listening. You take a little joy out of every win a friend shares.

angles.drive: You spend for show whenever the table is watching. Picking up the bill feels like winning the night, so you pay for everyone rather than let a rival treat you. You were buying a place at the table that was already yours.
angles.cost_self: Spending for show costs more than the bill says. You put the big gesture before the quiet balance, because being seen to give beats being secure. You are allowed to be generous in private.
angles.cost_others: Whenever a friend reaches for the bill, you are already spending for show. Paying matters more than letting them have a turn, so you take their round. You leave them no chance to be generous back with you.

angles.drive: You are never off, because off feels like falling behind. You would rather run past everyone than stop and ask who was racing you, since you see no finish. As the only one timing this race, you are free to call it done.
angles.cost_self: Never being off is your pride and what wears you down. You keep the pace up rather than admit you are tired, because tired looks like losing. Later you repay every skipped rest, and at a higher price.
angles.cost_others: Even with friends, you stay switched on and hand them a race instead of yourself. Being ahead counts more with you than being beside someone, so you set the pace even on a walk. You keep from them a friend with nothing to prove.

edge.lead: Fire runs through your wealth, your social life and your career. It is the big ask you make before fear catches up, the quiet party that comes alive when you walk in, and the bid you raise because someone else wants the same prize.
